reasons: The lake record is verified and identifies the case as Saucier v. Katz, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2001-06-18.
The disclosed citations match the asserted official, parallel, and vendor-neutral citations.
The disclosed treatment record shows caution/limited treatment, but no overrule, abrogation, supersession, or vacatur.
residual_risks: Currency is only verifiable from the disclosed lake treatment as of 2026-06-30.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Pair the citation with the Pearson limitation warning wherever the case is used for the mandatory sequencing rule.

reasons: Support merits are outside Lens B, and no disclosed treatment record undermines placing this case under qualified immunity.
The lake treatment record identifies later qualified-immunity refinement by Pearson through a limited-treatment edge.
residual_risks: The editorial strength of the word Key was not separately tested under Lens B.

reasons: The asserted holding is framed historically as the then-mandatory sequence.
The lake scope note confirms Pearson made Saucier's two-step sequence no longer mandatory while preserving the two-part qualified-immunity test.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity are outside Lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep every rule statement in historical terms or expressly qualify it with Pearson's no-longer-mandatory treatment.

reasons: The lake point_override for legacy-limited-saucier-v-katz matches the asserted caution validity, provisional binding status, Pearson cite, Pearson cluster_id, and field_ii limited label.
The lake treatment edges also include Pearson v. Callahan, 555 U.S. 223, with field_ii limited.
residual_risks: The override is marked provisional in the disclosed record.

defect.problem: The structured treatment fields survive, but the rendered page labels the overall status as limited while the lake field_i_validity is caution. Limited is the Pearson field_ii treatment event, not the overall field_i validity label.
defect.proposed_fix: Render the overall status as caution as of 2026-06-30, while separately stating that Pearson limited the mandatory-sequence point.

reasons: The lake treatment.field_i_validity is caution as of 2026-06-30.
The lake scope note supports the substance: Pearson made the sequence no longer mandatory, and the two-part test survives.
The lake also contains a proposed questioned edge from Vincent, which does not contradict caution but is not surfaced in the page narrative.
residual_risks: The treatment derivation relies on migrated treatment fields and a provisional point override.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Distinguish the overall validity label from the specific limiting treatment by Pearson.

reasons: The lake identity fields identify the court as the U.S. Supreme Court with court_id scotus and court_level scotus.
The caution/limited treatment affects the current force of the mandatory-sequence point, not the source-court weight of the decision.
residual_risks: The binding label should not be read to mean the pre-Pearson mandatory sequence remains binding.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Display Binding — SCOTUS together with the caution/Pearson limitation caveat.
